title: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: hunt on Microsoft Teams calls and meetings
summary: The briefing's licensing, call metadata, retention and roadmap facts are supported. Minor corrections should complete the permissions route and automation note, acknowledge conflicting Graph documentation, and identify the checklist's custom-detection control that has no table row.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes security admins with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 hunting on Teams calls and meetings for their organisation.
claims.quote: Security admins with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 can hunt on calls and meetings made inside Microsoft Teams for their organization

claims.claim: Call and meeting hunting is included in the extra Teams capabilities of Microsoft 365 E5 and Defender for Office 365 Plan 2.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5 and Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 extend Teams protection with a set of extra capabilities designed to disrupt the attack chain:

claims.claim: The comparison table marks advanced hunting on Teams calls and meetings for Plan 2, not Plan 1 or all Teams licences.

claims.claim: The Teams support page publishes no separate price for this capability.
claims.quote: Searched: CallActivityEvents Teams calls advanced hunting default enable disable licensing permissions retention. Opened and read mdo-support-teams-about, including its feature comparison and configuration sections; no separate call-hunting price appears.

claims.claim: The Teams support page publishes no separate meter for this capability.
claims.quote: Searched: CallActivityEvents Teams calls advanced hunting default enable disable licensing permissions retention. Read mdo-support-teams-about in full; it lists the Plan 2 capability without a separate usage meter.

claims.claim: CallActivityEvents is an advanced hunting table containing activities during Teams calls and meetings.
claims.quote: You can hunt across activities performed during Microsoft Teams calls and meetings using the CallActivityEvents advanced hunting table.

claims.claim: The table has an activity-type column.
claims.quote: | `ActivityType` | `string` | Type of activity performed during the call |

claims.claim: The table has an activity-status column.
claims.quote: | `ActivityStatus` | `string` | Success or failure of the activity performed |

claims.claim: The table records the activity timestamp.
claims.quote: | `ActivityTimestamp` | `datetime` | Date and time when the activity was recorded |

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The table contains the initiator's user principal name.
claims.quote: | `ActivityInitiatorUpn` | `string` | User principal name of the participant who initiated the activity |

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The table contains the initiator's display name.
claims.quote: | `ActivityInitiatorDisplayName` | `string` | Display name of the participant who initiated the activity |

claims.claim: The table contains the recipient's account identifier.
claims.quote: | `ActivityRecipientUpn` | `string` | Unique identifier for the account of the activity recipient |

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The table contains the initiator's phone number.
claims.quote: | `ActivityInitiatorPhoneNumber` | `string` | Third-party or Microsoft Teams phone number of the caller's account |

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The table contains the recipient's phone number.
claims.quote: | `ActivityRecipientPhoneNumber` | `string` | Third-party or Microsoft Teams phone number of the activity recipient |

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The table contains call join URLs.
claims.quote: | `CallJoinUrl` | `string` | Link that participants use to join the call |

claims.claim: The table contains the call name.
claims.quote: | `CallName` | `string` | Name of the call as displayed in the calendar invite |

claims.claim: The table contains the call scheduling type.
claims.quote: | `CallSchedulingType` | `string` | Type of scheduling for the call, such as `Adhoc`, `Scheduled`, or `Recurring` |

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The table contains the initiator's tenant name.
claims.quote: | `ActivityInitiatorTenantDisplayName` | `string` | Name of the organization that the activity initiator belongs to |

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure

claims.claim: Defender for Office 365 records populate the table.
claims.quote: This advanced hunting table is populated by records from Microsoft Defender for Office 365.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope
claims.claim: Queries fail or return no results if Defender for Office 365 is not deployed in Microsoft Defender.
claims.quote: If your organization hasn't deployed the service in Microsoft Defender, queries that use the table don't work or return any results.

claims.claim: Learn documents the table in the October 2026 What's new section, despite the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote:
## October 2026

- **Hunt across activities in Microsoft Teams calls and meetings**: The [CallActivityEvents table](/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-callactivityevents-table)

claims.claim: Microsoft says the table helps security teams investigate suspicious call activity.
claims.quote: helping security teams investigate suspicious call activity.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Advanced hunting queries can be reused to build custom detection rules.
claims.quote: You can use the same threat hunting queries to build custom detection rules.

claims.claim: Custom detection rules run automatically.
claims.quote: These rules run automatically to check for and then respond to suspected breach activity, misconfigured machines, and other findings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Native Defender advanced hunting data retention is up to 30 days by default.
claims.quote: Advanced hunting supports up to 30 days of native Defender data retention by default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Supported data has up to 90 days of retention with eligible ISOC licensing.
claims.quote: With ISOC, customers who have an eligible Microsoft Defender Suite, Microsoft 365 E5, or Microsoft 365 E7 license receive 90 days of included retention for supported Microsoft Defender data, Azure Activity data, and Office 365 Activity data.

claims.claim: CallActivityEvents is explicitly included in the ISOC retention benefit.
claims.quote:
The following tables and data sources are currently included:
- **Microsoft Defender for Office 365**
    - `CallActivityEvents`

claims.claim: The ISOC included retention benefit starts November 15, 2026.
claims.quote: Starting November 15, 2026, eligible customers receive up to 90 days of included retention for supported Microsoft Defender data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Advanced hunting queries require assigned permissions.
claims.quote: You need to be assigned permissions before you can run advanced hunting queries.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Defender unified RBAC is a documented route to advanced hunting access.
claims.quote: **Advanced Hunting access (Email & Collaboration tables)**: Membership assigned with the **Security operations** > **Raw data** > **Email & collaboration metadata (read)**URBAC permission.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Defender for Office 365 Email & collaboration role groups provide advanced hunting access to email tables.
claims.quote:
Membership in one of the following Email & Collaboration role groups provides access to email data tables in advanced hunting:
- Security Administrator
- Security Operator
- Security Reader

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Exchange Online role groups are another access route for Exchange Online data surfaced in advanced hunting.
claims.quote: To access Exchange Online data surfaced in advanced hunting, users must be members of one of the following Exchange Online role groups:

claims.claim: The overview lists Global Administrator, Security Administrator, Security Reader and Global Reader as Microsoft Entra roles granting full advanced hunting read access.
claims.quote:
Membership in one of the following Microsoft Entra roles grants full read access to all advanced hunting data:

- Security Administrator
- Security Reader

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The advanced hunting overview's table list for Email & collaboration metadata (read) does not name CallActivityEvents.
claims.quote: Searched: "CallActivityEvents" "default" enable disable hunting permissions ActivityType. Read advanced-hunting-overview Get access and custom-permissions-details; the overview's Email & collaboration metadata table list omits CallActivityEvents.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Hunting queries inspect the table's call metadata rather than taking action on calls.
claims.quote: Advanced hunting is a query-based threat hunting tool that you use to explore up to 30 days of raw Defender data, or up to 90 days of supported data with an eligible Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) license.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap and Learn description of this item state no automated action on calls or end-user behaviour change.
claims.quote: Searched: "CallActivityEvents" "custom detection"; "CallActivityEvents" "enable" "default" Teams hunting. Read roadmap, table schema, Teams support, What's new and hunting overview; no item-specific call remediation or end-user behaviour change stated.

claims.claim: The advanced hunting overview gives a result-set quota of 100,000 rows per query.
claims.quote: | Result set | 100,000 rows | Every query | Each query can return up to 100,000 records. |

claims.claim: The advanced hunting overview gives a ten-minute query timeout.
claims.quote: | Timeout | 10 minutes | Every query | Each query can run for up to 10 minutes. If it doesn't complete within 10 minutes, the service displays an error. |

claims.claim: Microsoft Defender portal > Permissions > Microsoft Defender XDR > Roles > Create custom role > Choose permissions reaches role permissions.
claims.quote:
On the Permissions page, under Microsoft Defender XDR, select Roles > Create custom role.
On the Choose permissions page, select each of the following as needed to configure permissions for that area:
claims.fix: The route stops on the permissions-selection page. For the general Email & collaboration hunting permission, give 'Permissions > Microsoft Defender XDR > Roles > Create custom role > Choose permissions > Security operations > Raw data > Email & collaboration metadata (read)', using https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-overview for the last permission levels. Keep the existing qualification that the overview's table list does not name CallActivityEvents.

claims.claim: POST /beta/roleManagement/defender/roleAssignments creates a Defender provider role assignment.
claims.quote:
To create role assignment for a Defender provider:
POST /roleManagement/defender/roleAssignments
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged and add to controls[0].note the properties already described in the prose: 'The request body sets roleDefinitionId for the assigned role and principalIds for the assigned users or groups.'

claims.claim: The beta Defender role-assignment API requires RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Defender.
claims.quote:
### For Defender provider
| Delegated (work or school account) | RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Defender | Not available. |
| Application | RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Defender | Not available. |

claims.claim: Defender unified RBAC must be activated before the portal enforces its configured permissions and assignments.
claims.quote: For the Microsoft Defender portal to start enforcing the permissions and assignments configured in your new or imported roles, you need to activate the new Microsoft Defender unified RBAC model.

claims.where: Governance controls: Assign users and data sources
claims.claim: After choosing role permissions, the wizard provides Assign users and data sources > Add assignment.
claims.quote: On the Assign users and data sources page, select Add assignment.

claims.claim: The assignment pane lets administrators select employees as users or security groups.
claims.quote: Employees: Select Microsoft Entra security groups or individual users to assign users to the role.

claims.claim: The assignment pane lets administrators select data sources.
claims.quote: Data sources: Select the Data sources drop down and then select the services where the assigned users will have the selected permissions.

claims.claim: Unless otherwise stated, unified RBAC permissions cover all supported workloads within the selected data scope.
claims.quote: Unless otherwise stated, all permissions are applicable to all supported workloads and will be applied to the data scope selected during the data source and assignment stage.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery lets applications run advanced hunting queries.
claims.quote:
Queries a specified set of event, activity, or entity data supported by Microsoft 365 Defender to proactively look for specific threats in your environment.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery

claims.claim: ThreatHunting.Read.All is a permission for runHuntingQuery.
claims.quote: | Application | ThreatHunting.Read.All | ThreatHunting.ReadWrite.All |

claims.claim: The runHuntingQuery reference does not name CallActivityEvents.
claims.quote: Searched: CallActivityEvents Teams calls advanced hunting default enable disable licensing permissions retention. Read the full v1.0 security-security-runhuntingquery reference, including examples; CallActivityEvents is not named.

claims.claim: roleDefinitionId identifies the role being assigned in the beta role-assignment request.
claims.quote: roleDefinitionId can be either the service-wide template ID or the directory-specific roleDefinitionId.

claims.claim: principalIds identifies the principals assigned to the role.
claims.quote: | principalIds | String collection | Identifiers of the principals to which the assignment is granted. Supports `$filter` (`any` operator only). |
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/unifiedroleassignmentmultiple?view=graph-rest-beta for the property definitions. Add: 'The create-operation reference lists the Defender provider, but the linked resource-type reference currently lists only Cloud PC and Microsoft Intune as supported providers.' Keep the documented beta Defender endpoint.

claims.claim: The CallActivityEvents table page names account types for call participants.
claims.quote: Classification of how the activity initiator is provisioned in the organization; possible values: Entra, consumer, Azure Communication Services, Public Switched Telephone Network, Unauthenticated

claims.claim: The table page does not enumerate the full list of ActivityType values.
claims.quote: Searched: "CallActivityEvents" "default" enable disable hunting permissions ActivityType. Read the full advanced-hunting-callactivityevents-table schema; ActivityType is described as 'Type of activity performed during the call' without an enumeration.
